result:
The admin API now shows a per-row count of unexpired access tokens, and has a new endpoint that revokes all tokens of one client while keeping the client. I did not run tests, lint, typecheck, or the app, as you asked. I also did not commit.

**What changed**

- **Count per row:** each item in `GET /mcp/oauth-clients` now has `activeAccessTokens`. It counts the access tokens for that client and owner whose expiry is still in the future. In the "mine" view that is your own grant. In the "all" view it is per owner.
- **Revoke endpoint:** `DELETE /mcp/oauth-clients/:clientId/tokens` requires `mcp:manage`. It deletes every access and refresh token of the client, for all users. It keeps the client and its consents, and returns `{ success, revokedAccessTokens, revokedRefreshTokens }`. A missing client, or a first-party client, returns 404.

**Why a migration was needed**

The access token table had no expiry column. Validity lives only in the JWT `exp` claim, so counting "still valid" in SQL needed a stored expiry. I added `expiresAt` (bigint, ms) to `oauth_access_tokens`, set on every insert. Verification still uses the JWT, so auth behaviour is unchanged.

**Files**

- `packages/@n8n/db/src/migrations/common/1795305600123-AddExpiresAtToOAuthAccessTokens.ts` (new)
- `packages/cli/src/modules/oauth-server/`: the entity, both token repositories, the token service, the server service, and the controller
- `packages/@n8n/api-types/src/dto/oauth/oauth-client.dto.ts` and `dto/index.ts`: new field and revoke response DTO
- `packages/cli/.../__tests__/oauth-token.service.test.ts`: one assertion updated for the new insert field
- `packages/modules/mcp/frontend/src/mcp.test.utils.ts`: fixture gets the new required field

**Choices I made that you may want to change**

- Existing access tokens get `expiresAt = 0`, so they count as expired until they are replaced. Verification is unaffected.
- The revoke runs two deletes without a transaction. This matches the existing `revokeAllTokensForGrant`. A retry fixes a partial failure.
- Revoked users are not shown as disconnected. Their consent stays, so they re-authorize silently on their next request.
- I did not add UI for the count or the revoke button. You asked for the admin API only.

**Things you need to do**

- The generated migration index (`src/migrations/{sqlite,postgresdb}/index.ts`) is not regenerated. I could not run `pnpm --filter=@n8n/db migration:new` (it was blocked), so I wrote the migration file by hand. Run `pnpm --filter=@n8n/db gen:migration-index`, or just run `pnpm build` or the package test script, which regenerate it. Plain `vitest` will fail the index sync check until you do.
- I could not check `git status` (the git commands needed approval). The list above comes from my own edits.
- Expired access-token rows are never deleted, so the table grows. That is a separate follow-up.
